title: PSG4-SECOND-SCALE: a two-scale base improves both exact time and source envelopes

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2N), L=log2n, the ONE PSG4-SECOND-SCALE program in proof.md uses the explicit exhaustive branch for n<256. Otherwise compute ell_base=ceil(log2n), g_base largest integer with g_base^8*ell_base^3<=n^4, g2_base largest integer with g2_base^16*ell_base^7<=n^8, and u=min(R,max(1,floor(R/3)+max(0,2g_base-floor(17g2_base/36)))). Use the first exact C4096 delta profile with2S_u(R)>=n, recomputing every q0,root,decoder,precision and BOTH actual acquisition and weighted-work caps. The complete selected fixed parameters are q=1/2,alpha=3/8,alpha2=7/16,eta=3/4. It recovers the entire secret from independent ideal copies with unconditional success at least1-2^-8>2/3. Jointly on EVERY branch including failed work, rejected/discarded copies, wrong labels, both aborts, initialization and cleanup, paid time T is O(2^((3/4)sqrt(nL)+(3/4)sqrt(n)L^(-3/8)-(1/24)sqrt(n)L^(-7/16))) with exact growth index1/2. All outside constants are absolute independent of N,s,outcomes. Every source, arithmetic, uniform circuit-generation, full indexed-address fee, measurement, reset, preprocessing, complete decoder, failed work and cleanup charge is paid jointly with both spaces, original copies, full-secret success and clean fraction0 for this same configuration.

For the same PSG4-SECOND-SCALE algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N>=2 and every s, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
